evidence_refs.description: HTTPServer.wait now loops around sleep without handling KeyboardInterrupt.
The base implementation caught KeyboardInterrupt and exited the wait loop cleanly.
The public run path advertises Ctrl+C shutdown and directly calls HTTPServer.wait.

findings.technical_rationale: This unrelated removal changes the documented synchronous server shutdown path: pressing Ctrl+C now lets KeyboardInterrupt escape from HTTPServer.wait and httpx.run instead of returning normally. Context-manager cleanup still runs, but normal interactive termination can now surface an exception/traceback to callers and scripts.
findings.comment_usefulness_rationale: A comment is useful because restoring the small KeyboardInterrupt guard preserves the existing public shutdown behavior without affecting the parser readiness fix.

review_summary: Reviewed the exact base-to-head diff locally. The parser readiness additions preserve buffered data and correctly distinguish EOF, but the same change also introduces one supported low-severity regression in synchronous Ctrl+C shutdown behavior.
